label: vanilla-percapita-n3
_why:
VANILLA GDP PER CAPITA for developed countries, which no existing session can give. 20260801_001026_vanilla-n3-v5 ran this exact span with country_state but WITHOUT the population metric, so its GDP figures can never be turned into per-capita — and the only long unbroken vanilla series in it is the USA, which is still 46% peasant in 1935 and is therefore not a developed economy at all. That gap is what makes the mod's output ladder impossible to calibrate: we do not know how rich a peasantless vanilla leader actually is. Adding `population` (which rides inside the same every_country pass as GDP, so it costs one extra debug_log per country per dump, not a second sweep) closes it.

Also carries `wages` for the per-pop-type table, i.e. people by PROFESSION, and keeps `market_goods` so that GDP and total market orders can be checked against each other on the SAME run — the open question of whether the two are interchangeable for calibration cannot be answered from two different sessions.

Tags and dump dates are IDENTICAL to 20260801_001026_vanilla-n3-v5 so the two are directly comparable and the new run can be read as that session plus population.
_analysis_note: DE-EMPHASISE GREAT BRITAIN when reading this. Its subject system means most of its economy and population sit in the British Market rather than the country, so its per-capita figures describe an empire, not the kind of single developed economy the era scenarios model. Prefer FRA / PRU / GER / NGF / AUS, and treat USA with care (46% peasant in 1935 in the earlier vanilla run — developed by GDP, not by structure).
